findings.title: Migration aborts on any database where `embed_category` was never set, because `[0]['id']` is called on an empty result
findings.description: The first query returns a row only when `site_settings` has an explicit `embed_category` row whose value matches a category name. Nothing writes that row: a grep of `db/` finds `embed_category` only in this migration, and `db/fixtures/001_categories.rb` seeds only `uncategorized_category_id`. On such a database `execute(...)` returns an empty result, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The `uncategorized_category_id` fallback at lines 14-16 is therefore unreachable there, and `db:migrate` stops. The tree has no `db/schema.rb` or `structure.sql`, so fresh databases also have to run this migration. The lookup needs a guard for the zero-row case before anything else.

findings.title: Legacy host entries are copied verbatim, so entries with a scheme or a trailing carriage return never match
findings.description: `val.split("\n")` inserts each line as-is. Raw SQL skips the `before_validation` that strips `https?://` (embeddable_host.rb:5-8). The removed `allows_embeddable_host?` accepted scheme-prefixed entries, so existing installs may have them. After migration, a row `https://blog.example.com` never equals the bare host that `record_for_host` compares against (embeddable_host.rb:14-17), and embeds from that site fail with `InvalidAccess` (embed_controller.rb:61). CRLF input also leaves `\r` in the stored host. The locale help text says hostname-only (e.g., config/locales/server.he.yml:984), so this affects only sites on the older format, but nothing normalizes it on upgrade.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
findings.description: The validator on line 2 accepts an optional `:port`, and `before_validation` keeps it. `record_for_host` looks up `uri.host` (line 14), which drops the port, against `lower(host)` (line 17). A row stored as `example.com:8080` never equals any lookup value. The admin sees a successful save, and the site is silently refused.

findings.title: The host lookup does not downcase the request host, although the validator is case-insensitive
findings.description: Ruby's URI keeps the host's case, so `uri.host` (line 14) reaches `lower(host) = ?` (line 17) unchanged. A request for `http://Blog.Example.com/` misses a stored `blog.example.com`. The validator (line 2, `/i`) also accepts mixed-case input, so mixed-case rows can be stored. Browsers lowercase Referer hosts, so the practical reach is `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, which passes the raw `@embed_url` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:16), and direct callers. `TopicEmbed.import` is unaffected because `normalize_url` downcases first (topic_embed.rb:10, 27).

findings.title: The format regex rejects valid hostnames whose top-level domain is longer than five letters
findings.description: `\.[a-z]{2,5}` cannot match a final label such as `community`, `technology`, or `international`. The old free-text setting accepted these, and the new validator blocks adding or re-saving them.

findings.title: Duplicate hosts are accepted, so the category a host gets depends on which row `first` returns
findings.description: There is no uniqueness validation (lines 1-3) and no unique index in the migration, so the same host can be added twice with different categories. `record_for_host` calls `where(...).first` with no `order`, so the category a topic is posted to is arbitrary.

findings.title: Updating or deleting an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns 500 instead of 404
findings.description: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and the same holds for the lookup on line 15. `save_host(nil)` then calls `nil.host=` (line 23), and `destroy` calls `nil.destroy` (line 16). A stale admin tab that tries to delete an already-removed host gets a server error.

findings.title: A missing `host` parameter crashes validation with NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error
findings.description: `save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, which is nil when the key is omitted. `before_validation` then calls `self.host.sub!` on nil, raising NoMethodError inside `valid?`. The column is `null: false`, so the intended response is a validation error.

findings.title: A failed host delete is silently swallowed
findings.description: The save path ends with `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (line 40), but the delete chain `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no catch. The frontend has no global RSVP error handler: a grep of `app/assets/javascripts` for `RSVP.on(`, `RSVP.configure`, and `Ember.onerror` returns nothing. A failed DELETE leaves the row on screen and shows the admin no message.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns success and persists nothing
findings.description: `update` re-renders `@embedding` without calling any save, so a client gets a 200 and no change. The route is live (config/routes.rb:139). The only caller is `saveChanges` in `admin-embedding.js.es6`, and no template binds it, so the practical exposure is direct API calls.

findings.title: Imports for hosts not in the list lose the `embed_category` fallback and get no category
findings.description: Previously `TopicEmbed.import` posted new topics to `SiteSetting.embed_category`. Now it looks up the host and passes `eh.try(:category_id)`, which is nil for any URL whose host isn't listed. `Jobs::PollFeed#import_topic` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:39) passes every feed item URL with no host filter, so feed topics from unlisted hosts are uncategorized. Sites that relied on the global fallback lose it.
